newsitem.title: USA: Occidental Q1 oil and gas unit earnings up.
newsitem.headline: Occidental Q1 oil and gas unit earnings up.

text.p: Occidental Petroleum Thursday said its first-quarter oil and gas divisional earnings rose to $228 million from $161 million because of higher worldwide crude oil and natural gas prices and cost benefits from the reorganization.
These were partially offset by higher taxes, depreciation and exploration expense.

Natural gas transmission divisional earnings for the first quarter of 1997 were $91 million, compared with $121 million for 1996. The decline in 1997 earnings resulted primarily from lower margins on sales and transportation, partially offset by reduced costs.

In announcing the results, Ray Irani, chairman and chief executive officer, stated, "Our improved earnings in the first quarter of 1997 reflect higher oil and gas prices. We continue our strategy to increase earnings by growing our core businesses while reducing debt and operating costs."
